# Honeywell Aerospace Inc. (HONA)
Analysis date: 2026-11-14

Data limitation: No annual 10-K facts established; quarterly facts are not annualized.

## Overview

- Honeywell Aerospace is a leading global tier‑1 aerospace and defense supplier of mission‑critical systems and technologies that support OEMs, governments, defense prime contractors and aircraft operators across commercial air transport, business aviation and defense & space markets. — 10-Q line 879: We are a leading global tier-1 aerospace and defense supplier of mission critical systems and technologies that enable the production, maintenance, and safe operation of aerospace and defense platforms. Our systems and technologies support original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”), government, defense prime contractors, and aircraft operator customers across the Commercial Air Transport, Business Aviation, and Defense and Space end markets. Our comprehensive portfolio of market leading systems and technologies are organized into the following segments: Electronic Solutions (“ES”), Engines & Power Systems (“E&PS”), and Control Systems (“CS”).
- The company became an independent public company on June 29 2026 through a pro‑rata spin‑off of all its outstanding common shares. — 10-Q line 881: On June 29, 2026 (the “Distribution Date”), Honeywell completed the spin‑off of the Aerospace Business (the “Spin‑off”) through a pro‑ra‑distribution (the “Distribution”) of all of our outstanding common shares to holders of record of Honeywell's common shares as of the close of business on June 15, 2026 (the “Record Date”), at which time each holder of Honeywell's common shares received one Aerospace common share for every two Honeywell common shares held as of the close of business on the Record Date, resulting in the Distribution of 316.9 million of our common shares.

- Backlog at quarter end was $19.3 billion, up 12 % from the prior year, providing a sizable order pipeline. — EX-99.1 line 38: Backlog | | $19,324 | | $17,255 | | 12%
- Trailing twelve‑month orders grew 9 % year‑over‑year, led by the Defense and Space segment. — EX-99.1 line 36: Honeywell Aerospace sales for the third quarter increased 2% on a reported and organic¹ basis year over year. Backlog grew to $19.3 billion at quarter end, up 12% from the prior year, and trailing twelve‑months orders were up 9%, led by Defense and Space.
- Commercial Original Equipment sales grew 7 % on a reported basis (8 % organically) in Q3 2026. — EX-99.1 line 50: % Organic1 Commercial Original Equipment | | $690 | | $642 | | 7% | | 8%
- Management maintains full‑year organic sales growth guidance of 4 %–5 % for 2026. — EX-99.1 line 56: Organic1,4 growth | | 4% - 5% | | 4% - 5%

## Valuation Insights

The quarterly filing reports the company’s operating results for the third quarter ending in late September, including sales, net income, earnings per share and free cash flow, but the XBRL facts for key GAAP concepts are absent, preventing verification and ratio computation.
The release highlights a new dividend declaration, a modest increase in backlog, and an upward revision to full‑year adjusted earnings guidance, yet the company does not provide a GAAP reconciliation for its non‑GAAP earnings measures.
The balance sheet shows a significant increase in long‑term debt relative to the prior period, but without tagged debt figures the debt‑to‑equity relationship cannot be quantified.
Liquidity is described as strong, with cash and cash equivalents rising sharply, but the lack of tagged cash‑flow items means the sustainability of operating cash generation cannot be assessed.
Because a market price, its date and source, and the earnings denominator are not supplied, any valuation multiples are outside the permissible scope.
Peer comparison is not possible as no peer financial data with matching periods are available.
The filing notes that the company’s fiscal calendar closes on a Saturday for the third quarter, establishing the reporting period for the disclosed results.

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

- The company announced a 300,000 sq ft expansion of its Tempe, Arizona manufacturing facility, slated to open in late 2028, to add capacity and improve supply‑chain resilience. — EX-99.1 line 33: The company announced a 300,000 square foot expansion of its Tempe, Arizona manufacturing facility, expected to open in late 2028. The new facility adds capacity, lean manufacturing, automation, and supply-chain resilience to support current Control Systems production, recent wins, and next generation platforms.
- Supply‑chain conditions remain varied, with constraints in skilled labor, manufacturing capacity and sub‑tier supply availability affecting delivery and cost. — 10-Q line 891: Within Honeywell Aerospace, supply conditions remain varied, with certain suppliers continuing to experience constraints in skilled labor, manufacturing capacity, and sub‑tier supply availability, as well as quality and delivery execution challenges.
- The company will pay Honeywell $1.125 billion over five years for the usage of the Honeywell Aerospace trademark. — 10-Q line 403: In exchange, the Company will pay Honeywell an aggregate amount of $1,125 million over a period of five years, with an initial payment of $18.75 million that was paid within five days of the Distribution Date followed by 59 equal monthly payments of $18.75 million.
- In connection with the spin‑off, the company issued $16.0 billion of senior unsecured notes in nine series maturing between 2028 and 2066. — 10-Q line 498: On March 16, 2026, and in connection with the Spin‑off, the Company issued an aggregate of $16.0 billion principal amount of the Initial Notes in nine series with maturity dates ranging from 2028 through 2066.
- Risk factors include changes in raw‑material prices and supplier ability to meet quality and delivery requirements, which could disrupt production. — 10-Q line 141: changes in the price and availability of raw materials that we use to produce our products, including the ability of suppliers to meet quality and delivery requirements and our ability to reduce the impact of such disruptions
- Judgment: Leverage the new Tempe facility to offset identified supply‑chain constraints and improve delivery reliability. — 10-Q line 33: The company announced a 300,000 square foot expansion of its Tempe, Arizona manufacturing facility, expected to open in late 2028.
- Judgment: Preserve ample liquidity given the $15.9 billion long‑term debt load and recent increase in interest expense (line 187) and transaction‑cost cash outflows (line 376). — 10-Q line 187: Interest expense (income), net 187

## Investment Recommendation

**Insufficient evidence** — Honeywell Aerospace has successfully spun off as a standalone tier‑1 supplier and reports a growing order backlog and maintained organic sales guidance. However, the company now carries a substantial new senior‑note debt load, faces continued supply‑chain constraints, and incurs ongoing trademark‑license payments. The lack of disclosed quantitative growth rates and margins prevents a clear assessment of profitability and valuation, leaving the investment case uncertain.
Deciding metric unavailable; the recommendation cannot be assessed against its selected calculation.
- Risk: Supply‑chain constraints could impair delivery and increase costs.
- Risk: High leverage from the recent senior‑note issuance may limit financial flexibility.
- Risk: Trademark‑license payments to Honeywell add a recurring expense.
- Risk: Macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical tensions could affect demand.
- Risk: Litigation and other contingent liabilities could materialize unexpectedly.
Backlog at quarter end was $19.3 billion, up 12 % from the prior year, providing a sizable order pipeline — EX-99.1 line 38: “Backlog | | $19,324 | | $17,255 | | 12%”

## Evidence gaps

- The filings do not disclose quantitative market‑share percentages or rankings relative to peers; therefore any claim about market‑share position cannot be substantiated.
- No forward‑looking quantitative guidance is provided for segment‑level sales growth beyond the aggregate organic growth range; detailed segment forecasts are absent.
- There is no disclosed capital‑allocation plan for potential acquisitions beyond the generic statement that the company evaluates targets (see MD&A line 1152).
- The MD&A does not provide a timeline for the completion of the Transition Services Agreement beyond the general two‑year window; specifics on cost transition are missing.
- The 10‑Q does not contain a detailed sensitivity analysis for the impact of higher interest rates on debt service; such information would be needed to fully assess financing risk.
- No explicit statement on competitive pricing strategy or differentiation beyond generic technology leadership is present; thus claims about pricing advantage cannot be sourced.
- The earnings release does not quantify the expected impact of the trademark‑license payments on margin; the $1.125 billion total is disclosed but annual expense effect is not broken out.
- There is no disclosed information on the expected timing or magnitude of cash‑flow benefits from the Tempe expansion; the claim about capacity increase is qualitative.
- The risk‑factors section lists many potential threats, but the 10‑Q does not quantify the probability or financial impact of each, limiting risk‑assessment specificity.
- All required XBRL concept tags (revenue, operating income, net income, EPS, debt, cash from operations, etc.) are null, limiting the ability to perform any quantitative analysis or construct financial ratios.
- No market price information is provided, so price‑to‑earnings or other valuation multiples cannot be calculated.
- Peer data is absent, so relative performance cannot be benchmarked.
- The non‑GAAP measures are presented without a detailed reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, restricting the reliability of those supplemental figures.
- The filing does not include a full 10‑K or audited annual statements, so annual trends and year‑over‑year comparisons are constrained to the quarterly snapshot.

168: ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE INC.
169: Honeywell Aerospace Inc. (“Honeywell Aerospace”, “Aerospace”, “we”, “us”, or “our”) is an independent global aerospace and defense company whose critical technologies are broadly deployed on the world’s leading commercial air transport, business aviation, defense and space platforms. These integrated solutions enable safer, more efficient, and more reliable missions. With a broad portfolio spanning avionics and navigation systems, engines and power systems, and control systems for aircraft, Honeywell Aerospace combines commitment and deep engineering expertise to drive innovation and long-term value for the aerospace industry. Our comprehensive portfolio of market leading systems and technologies are organized into three reportable segments: Electronic Solutions, Engines & Power Systems, and Control Systems.
170: Our SEC filings, including our Information Statement, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, and any amendments to those reports, are available free of charge on our Investor Relations website (investor.honeywellaerospace.com) immediately after they are filed with, or furnished to, the SEC. 877: OVERVIEW
878: Business Overview
879: We are a leading global tier-1 aerospace and defense supplier of mission critical systems and technologies that enable the production, maintenance, and safe operation of aerospace and defense platforms. Our systems and technologies support original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”), government, defense prime contractors, and aircraft operator customers across the Commercial Air Transport, Business Aviation, and Defense and Space end markets. Our comprehensive portfolio of market leading systems and technologies are organized into the following segments: Electronic Solutions (“ES”), Engines & Power Systems (“E&PS”), and Control Systems (“CS”).
880: Spin-off from Honeywell
881: On June 29, 2026 (the “Distribution Date”), Honeywell completed the spin-off of the Aerospace Business (the “Spin-off”) through a pro-rata distribution (the “Distribution”) of all of our outstanding common shares to holders of record of Honeywell's common shares as of the close of business on June 15, 2026 (the “Record Date”), at which time each holder of Honeywell's common shares received one Aerospace common share for every two Honeywell common shares held as of the close of business on the Record Date, resulting in the Distribution of 316.9 million of our common shares. Upon completion of the Distribution, we became an independent public company. Our common stock is listed under the symbol “HONA” on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”).
882: Relationship with Honeywell
883: Prior to the Spin-off, the financial statements included herein were derived from Honeywell’s historical accounting records and presented on a standalone basis as if our operations had been conducted independently from Honeywell in accordance with GAAP. The accompanying financial statements for periods prior to the Spin-off include certain assets and liabilities that have historically been held at the Honeywell corporate level but are specifically identifiable or otherwise attributable to us. Prior to the Spin-off, Honeywell provided certain services, such as legal, accounting, information technology, human resources, and other infrastructure support, on behalf of us. We consider allocations of these costs to be a reasonable reflection of the benefits we received. However, the financial information presented in the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements may not reflect our consolidated financial position, operating results, and cash flows had we been a separate standalone entity during the periods presented. Actual costs that would have been incurred if we had been a standalone company would depend on multiple factors, including organizational structure and strategic decisions made in various areas, including information technology and infrastructure. We consider the basis on which the expenses have been allocated to be a reasonable reflection of the utilization of services provided to or the benefits received by us during the periods prior to the Spin-off.

888: We have incurred and expect to incur certain costs in connection with our establishment as a standalone public company (the “transaction costs”). The transaction costs include non-recurring expenses associated with the Spin-off and stand up of functions required to operate as a standalone public entity. These non-recurring costs primarily relate to system implementation costs, business and facilities separation, applicable employee-related costs, the evolution of our brand, and other matters. The transaction costs are expected to continue through at least fiscal year 2027. Additionally, we have incurred and will further incur increased costs as a result of becoming an independent, publicly traded company, primarily from establishing or expanding the corporate support for our businesses, including IT, human resources, treasury, tax, internal audit, risk management, stock-based compensation programs, accounting and financial reporting, investor relations, governance, legal, procurement, and other services.
889: Macroeconomic Conditions
890: We continue to monitor elevated macroeconomic and geopolitical developments, including armed conflict in the Middle East and its effects on global energy markets and maritime shipping, evolving U.S. trade policy and tariff authorities, inflationary pressures, and financial market uncertainty. Moderated global growth projections and tariffs imposed during 2025 and 2026, together with evolving U.S. trade policy and international negotiations, contributed to increased volatility across global supply chains. Elevated energy prices, tariff-related cost impacts, and continued market uncertainty may continue to contribute to supply chain disruptions, cost inflation, and pricing volatility. We continue to work proactively with our suppliers and customers to mitigate shortages, maintain supply continuity, and manage cost impacts.
891: Within Honeywell Aerospace, supply conditions remain varied, with certain suppliers continuing to experience constraints in skilled labor, manufacturing capacity, and sub-tier supply availability, as well as quality and delivery execution challenges. These conditions can limit suppliers’ ability to support production requirements and recover past-due deliveries, and contribute to lead-time uncertainty and cost pressures. We continue to address these challenges through direct engagement with critical suppliers, targeted supplier development and recovery plans, production-rate and capacity validation, improved demand and supply planning, long-term supply agreements, and selective inventory investments. Where feasible, we are also pursuing alternate-source qualification and design changes to improve supply resilience. The timing and effectiveness of these actions depend on supplier execution and applicable engineering, qualification, and customer approval requirements, which can limit our ability to transition supply in the near term. We have also announced the planned expansion of our manufacturing facilities in Tempe, Arizona. These measures are intended to improve supply continuity and support customer commitments while maintaining product quality and reliability; however, supply constraints and associated cost pressures may persist.
892: To date, these actions have mitigated some of the effects of these conditions; however, supply chain constraints continue to affect certain aspects of our business and may continue to do so in future periods. Their continued effectiveness depends on successful execution, the availability of alternative sources of supply and the duration and severity of the underlying market conditions. If these conditions worsen or our mitigation efforts prove insufficient, our results of operations, cash flows, or financial condition could be materially adversely affected.

22: PHOENIX, October 28, 2026 -- Honeywell Aerospace (Nasdaq: HONA) today announced results for the third quarter and declared its first quarterly dividend. The company also raised its full-year 2026 pro forma standalone adjusted earnings per share1 and second half 2026 free cash flow1 guidance ranges, maintained its full-year organic1 sales outlook, and narrowed its full-year pro forma standalone adjusted EBIT1 guidance range.
23: “Honeywell Aerospace delivered results above our expectations in its first quarter as a standalone company, increasing sales and adjusted EBIT sequentially and year over year as we accelerate investments to drive greater output and better serve our customers. Demand for our solutions remains robust with 9% orders growth over the last 12 months,” said Jim Currier, Chief Executive Officer of Honeywell Aerospace. “We are seeing encouraging signs from pacing suppliers as we deepen our commitment to enduring partnerships. This progress, combined with ongoing qualification of additional material sources, positions us for higher sales and output growth in 2027 and beyond.”
24: Initial dividend declaration
25: Honeywell Aerospace’s Board of Directors has approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.40 per share of its common stock. The dividend is payable on December 4, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 13, 2026.
26: Currier added, “The Board’s decision to declare a regular dividend underscores the visibility into our durable free cash flow growth in the years ahead. Paying a competitive, growing dividend is a key component of our capital allocation strategy designed to deliver substantial shareholder value while maintaining financial flexibility and a strong investment-grade credit rating.”
27: Recent Honeywell Aerospace highlights
28: •Year to date, the company has secured more than $20 billion in new wins (estimated lifetime value) supported by the following announcements:
29: ◦The U.S. Air Force advanced Honeywell Aerospace’s SkyShot 1600 engine, which is designed to meet all mission-critical performance parameters for collaborative combat aircraft and unmanned aircraft systems, into Preliminary Design Review as part of its Autonomous Collaborative Platform program.
30: ◦Honeywell Aerospace secured over $2 billion in new awards to provide its advanced navigation and RF systems for several missiles and munitions programs, including some initial contracts on platforms prioritized by the Munitions Acceleration Council.
31: ◦The City of Phoenix Aviation Department signed an agreement with Honeywell Aerospace to study how to translate the company’s Surface Alert (SURF-A) technology to ground vehicle operators on tarmacs, taxiways, and runways at three local airports, including Phoenix Sky Harbor International.
32: Honeywell Aerospace 3Q26 Results - 2
33: •The company announced a 300,000 square foot expansion of its Tempe, Arizona manufacturing facility, expected to open in late 2028. The new facility adds capacity, lean manufacturing, automation, and supply-chain resilience to support current Control Systems production, recent wins, and next generation platforms.
34: •Honeywell Aerospace presented an update on its supply chain transformation at a September investor conference. Key messages from the presentation included root causes and actions underway for the constraints from a small number of mechanical suppliers currently limiting output growth.
35: Summary financial results
36: Honeywell Aerospace sales for the third quarter increased 2% on a reported and organic¹ basis year over year. Backlog grew to $19.3 billion at quarter end, up 12% from the prior year, and trailing twelve-months orders were up 9%, led by Defense and Space. Adjusted EBIT1 was up 1%, including both an approximately $50 million net benefit from International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refunds and new costs necessary as an independent public company.

13: With more than $17 billion in annual revenue for 2025 and a global installed base spanning virtually every commercial and defense aircraft platform, Honeywell Aerospace will be one of the largest publicly traded aerospace suppliers. Its leading positions across propulsion, cockpit and navigation systems, and auxiliary power, combined with a significant aftermarket business, provide a durable foundation for recurring revenue and long-term sustainable growth. With Jim Currier and his team in place and already executing for customers, Honeywell Aerospace has a strong foundation to build on Honeywell’s legacy of engineering excellence while accelerating its next phase of growth as a standalone company.
15: To learn more, I encourage you to read the attached information statement, which describes the spin-off in detail and contains important business and financial information. When the distribution occurs, each Honeywell shareowner will receive one share of Honeywell Aerospace for every two shares of Honeywell common stock held as of the close of business on June 15, 2026, the record date for the distribution. Those shares are expected to trade on NASDAQ under the ticker symbol “HONA,” and the spin-off is expected to be tax-free to Honeywell shareowners for U.S. federal income tax purposes (other than any cash that Honeywell shareowners receive in lieu of fractional shares). 24: Our business builds on more than a century of reliable performance and continuous innovation. We work closely with customers to anticipate needs, develop solutions and keep aircraft flying safely and efficiently. Our long track record, deep industry experience and cutting-edge technology position us as a trusted provider of advanced systems across the Commercial Air Transport, Business Aviation and Defense and Space end markets.

125: What is Aerospace and why is Honeywell separating the Aerospace Business and distributing Aerospace common stock?
126: Aerospace, which is currently a wholly owned subsidiary of Honeywell, was formed to own and operate Honeywell’s Aerospace Business. Honeywell intends to separate Aerospace from the rest of Honeywell by distributing all of the outstanding Aerospace common stock to Honeywell shareowners on a pro rata basis as of the record date for the distribution. The separation of Aerospace from Honeywell is intended, among other things, to better position the management of both companies to pursue opportunities for long-term growth and profitability unique to each company’s business and to allow each business to more effectively implement its own distinct capital structure and capital allocation strategies. Honeywell expects that the separation will result in enhanced long-term performance of each business for the reasons discussed in the section entitled “The Separation and Distribution—Reasons for the Separation.”
